reviews.reviewerId: scene-closure execution owner (Claude Opus 5 main session, openclinxr-c2)
reviews.observations: Reran every doneWhen in the integrated main checkout: foot-plant regressions 21/21, the named behavior test 1/1, assert-contract-live 1 contract live, verifier suite 21/21, typecheck:relaxed 0 errors, knip clean, biome clean over the cards files. Ran an own probe distinct from the implementer eight-break sweep: setting PERCEPTUAL_FLOOR_METERS to 0.12, a 24x widening of the root constant every perceptual threshold derives from, fails four clauses including SC-00-required-behavior and the stale-rubric corrupt control, so the report is bound to the recorded thresholds and a quiet widening is detected rather than absorbed; restoring passes 22 of 22. ACCEPTED THE CENTRAL FINDING AS A FAILURE OF THE ASSET, NOT OF THE CARD: the shipped openclinxr_retarget_walk_formal_cc0 violates foot-slide at 8.0x and 20.0x worst-frame on the left and right toe and 12.4x on left total, measured on the shipped bytes 4a6d8a78 rather than the pre-graft build sc-04.json graded, and the retired CMU clip would also have failed at 3.6x. The rubric was not widened to admit either. That is the outcome this card was dispatched to make possible and it is recorded in limits.unresolvedDefects; SC-05 inherits a stance-constraint problem rather than a clip-selection one. Verified the implementer own self-correction rather than taking it on report: two of its eight breaks passed on the first run because every control also failed on total slide and because a resweep step change was absorbed by a float accident, and both were closed by adding a single-frame-pop control and by asserting threshold values against their derivations. Also acted on two findings the implementer raised outside its scope: SC-01S behavior test imported the xr-station package by name, resolving to a gitignored dist, and reported no tests rather than failing when that dist was absent, with the root //#test:tools turbo task carrying no build dependency and running first; repaired at 6e68ab1e and probed with dist moved aside. Separately, the gitignored supine-control freeze refused after SC-04 republished the physician GLB; the one changed hash was re-recorded locally, and the freeze auto-initialises when absent, so on a clean clone that test passes trivially against whatever bytes are present.

unprovenClinical: No clinical validity claim. The thresholds here are engineering checks on geometry and timing; whether a pose or a gait is clinically appropriate needs qualified review, which has not happened.

The reach and access figures this rubric leans on (0.3 m footprint, 1.8 m standing height, 0.26 m foot length) are external adult anthropometric floors, not a validated clinical standard for any procedure.
unprovenHeadset: Every measurement here is offline geometry decoded from shipped bytes. Nothing was worn, rendered on a headset, or frame-paced.
unprovenPublication: No Pages push and no public claim. The perceptual floor is derived from the capture camera's framing, not from any published capture.
unresolvedDefects: THE SHIPPED LOCOMOTION CLIP FAILS THIS RUBRIC. openclinxr_retarget_walk_formal_cc0 on the shipped physician violates foot-slide at both the executor's 1.1 m/s advance and the clip's own 0.676 m/s stance-derived advance, by 8.0x and 20.0x on worst-frame slide for the left and right toe. It satisfies the other sixteen metrics. SC-05 owns the repair; the rubric was not widened to admit it.

The retired CMU 02_01 clip would also have failed: sc-04.json records its worst single-frame slide at 0.0181 m, 3.6x the 0.005 m allowance. No locomotion clip this pipeline has produced meets the plant threshold, so SC-05's remedy is foot-lock IK or an equivalent stance constraint, not a different clip.
mpfb-peds-parent-aisha.motion-bind.glb carries the same glTF-source orientation defect SC-04 found and fixed in its own bind path. Outside SC-00's scope and recorded so it is not rediscovered.

Support, route, arrival and settled heading have no shipped producer at this baseline. Their controls supply those sections from real measured dimensions and are labelled instrument controls; they are not evidence that any placement or run occurred.
